original_question: For every integer d >= 3 and every integer r with d/2 <= r <= d - 1, does there exist a maximal Tjurina curve of type (d, r), meaning a reduced degree-d plane curve C : f = 0 with mdr(f) = r that attains the sharp upper bound in equation (6.1)? Moreover, for d/2 <= r <= d - 2, do there also exist maximal Tjurina line arrangements of type (d, r)?
target_in_paper: Section 6, Conjecture 6.1, immediately after the definition of a maximal Tjurina curve of type (d,r) via equality (6.1); this is the exact statement your draft is trying to capture. ([imar.ro](https://imar.ro/journals/Revue_Mathematique/pdfs/2024/2/4.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s official existence conjecture almost verbatim: the quantifiers on d and r are correct, the notion of a maximal Tjurina curve of type (d,r) is used in the same sense as the paper (a reduced degree-d plane curve with mdr(f)=r attaining equality (6.1)), and the additional line-arrangement clause for d/2 ≤ r ≤ d−2 is exactly the second sentence of Conjecture 6.1. ([imar.ro](https://imar.ro/journals/Revue_Mathematique/pdfs/2024/2/4.pdf))
missing_details: To make the question stand-alone, the ambient setting should be stated explicitly: S = C[x,y,z], f is a homogeneous polynomial of degree d, and C = {f=0} is a reduced plane curve in P^2_C. ([imar.ro](https://imar.ro/journals/Revue_Mathematique/pdfs/2024/2/4.pdf))

The invariant mdr(f) should be defined from the Jacobian syzygy module AR(f)=D0(f)={(a,b,c)∈S^3 : af_x+bf_y+cf_z=0} as the minimal degree of a nonzero Jacobian syzygy. ([imar.ro](https://imar.ro/journals/Revue_Mathematique/pdfs/2024/2/4.pdf))

The phrase attains the sharp upper bound in equation (6.1) should be replaced by the explicit formula τ(C)=τ(d,r)_max−binom(2r+2−d,2), where τ(d,r)_max=(d−1)^2−r(d−r−1); otherwise the question depends on an internal equation label and is not self-contained. ([imar.ro](https://imar.ro/journals/Revue_Mathematique/pdfs/2024/2/4.pdf))
It should say that τ(C) is the total Tjurina number, i.e. the sum of the local Tjurina numbers of the singularities of C. ([imar.ro](https://imar.ro/journals/Revue_Mathematique/pdfs/2024/2/4.pdf))

For the second clause, maximal Tjurina line arrangement of type (d,r) should be spelled out as an arrangement of d lines in P^2_C whose defining reduced homogeneous polynomial f satisfies mdr(f)=r and the same equality for τ(C). ([imar.ro](https://imar.ro/journals/Revue_Mathematique/pdfs/2024/2/4.pdf))

No extra asymptotic qualifier such as sufficiently large d or sufficiently large m appears in the paper’s formulation, and there is no additional nilpotency or positive-characteristic hypothesis beyond the ambient complex setting. ([imar.ro](https://imar.ro/journals/Revue_Mathematique/pdfs/2024/2/4.pdf))
refined_question: Let S = C[x,y,z], let f ∈ S be homogeneous of degree d ≥ 3, and let C : f = 0 ⊂ P^2_C be a reduced plane curve. Write AR(f) = {(a,b,c) ∈ S^3 : af_x + bf_y + cf_z = 0} and mdr(f) = min{q : AR(f)_q ≠ 0}. For every integer r with d/2 ≤ r ≤ d−1, does there exist such a curve C with mdr(f)=r and total Tjurina number τ(C) = (d−1)^2 − r(d−r−1) − binom(2r+2−d,2), i.e. a maximal Tjurina curve of type (d,r)? Moreover, for every integer r with d/2 ≤ r ≤ d−2, can one choose C to be a line arrangement of d lines in P^2_C? ([imar.ro](https://imar.ro/journals/Revue_Mathematique/pdfs/2024/2/4.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, in the range d/2 ≤ r ≤ d−1, is the stronger du Plessis–Wall upper bound τ(C) ≤ τ(d,r)_max − binom(2r+2−d,2) sharp for every pair (d,r), and is it sharp within the class of line arrangements whenever d/2 ≤ r ≤ d−2? Here τ(d,r)_max = (d−1)^2 − r(d−r−1). ([imar.ro](https://imar.ro/journals/Revue_Mathematique/pdfs/2024/2/4.pdf))
justification: The draft is targeting Section 6 rather than the ADE-maximizing questions of Section 7. Section 1 says that Section 6 studies non-free curves attaining the du Plessis–Wall bounds. Section 2 fixes the ambient complex-projective setting and defines Jacobian syzygies and mdr(f), while Theorem 2.4 gives the stronger upper bound for τ(C) when r ≥ d/2. Section 6 then defines a maximal Tjurina curve of type (d,r) exactly by equality (6.1) and immediately states Conjecture 6.1 with the same two existence clauses as in your draft. So the draft is very close, but it is not fully stand-alone because it relies on the internal reference equation (6.1) and omits the ambient setup and explicit formula that the paper uses. ([imar.ro](https://imar.ro/journals/Revue_Mathematique/pdfs/2024/2/4.pdf))
